text: Theorem. The square root of 2 is irrational. Proof. Suppose sqrt(2) = p/q in lowest terms. Then p^2 = 2 q^2, so p^2 is even, hence p is even; write p = 2k. Substituting gives 4 k^2 = 2 q^2, so q^2 = 2 k^2 and q is also even. But then p and q share the factor 2, contradicting the assumption that p/q was in lowest terms. Therefore sqrt(2) cannot be written as a ratio of integers.

Theorem (AM-GM, n = 2). For nonnegative reals a and b, (a + b)/2 >= sqrt(ab), with equality iff a = b. Proof. Since squares are nonnegative, (sqrt(a) - sqrt(b))^2 >= 0. Expanding gives a - 2 sqrt(ab) + b >= 0, hence a + b >= 2 sqrt(ab), and dividing by 2 yields the claim. Equality holds exactly when sqrt(a) = sqrt(b), that is, when a = b.

Worked example: compute-optimal token budgets. Under the Chinchilla scaling heuristic of roughly 20 training tokens per parameter, a 627-billion-parameter dense model is compute-optimal near 12.5 trillion tokens. Training on 36 trillion tokens therefore sits at about 2.9 times the optimal point: total FLOPs follow 6ND = 6 x 6.27e11 x 3.6e13, approximately 1.35e26, and the marginal evaluation gain per FLOP diminishes but remains positive across the 20-40T band.
